text:
Blank
c. Blank

2010 QCCS 6311

SUPerior

JR1353

COURt

CANADA

PROVINCE
of QUÉBEC

DISTRICT
of

MONTREAL

N°:

500-17-033071-062

DATE :

December
16, 2010

_________________________________________________________________________

presiding:
the HONORABLE BRIAN RIORDAN, J.S.C.

_________________________________________________________________________

HEDY BLANK

Plaintiff

v.

HOWARD
BLANK

Defendant

_________________________________________________________________________

judgment

_________________________________________________________________________

THE PROCEEDINGS

[
1
]

Defendant ("
Howard
"
[1]
)
is the brother of Plaintiff ("
Hedy
").  The will of their
mother ("
mother
"), who died in September 2005, greatly
favoured Hedy over both Howard and their two brothers, Arthur and Sheldon.

[
2
]

None of Hedy's brothers were happy about the
contents of mother's will and they insisted that Hedy renounce it and have the
estate decided according to Jewish law before the Rabbinical Court, also known
as the
Beth Din
.  When she refused, Howard was particularly incensed and
he took several steps intended to coerce Hedy into submitting to the Beth Din,
or to punish her for not doing so.  In particular, he:

a.  set up a website called Hedystzoros.com (the
"
Website
");

b.

he telephoned the principal of the Orthodox
Jewish school (the "
Principal
") where Hedy has taught for some
35 years;

c.

he left menacing messages on her telephone voice
mail (the "
Messages
").

[
3
]

Hedy claims that these acts constitute
harassment, a violation of her fundamental rights and an invasion of her
privacy.  She claims moral damages in the amount of $25,000 and punitive
damages under the
Quebec
Charter of Human Rights and Freedoms
, R.S.Q.
ch. C-12 (the "
Charter
"), in the amount of $50,000.

[
4
]

Howard counters that he had every right to try
to convince her to compromise on the question of mother's will, whether by
mutual agreement or by submitting the question to the Beth Din.  He admits he
lost his temper and exaggerated in the Messages, but cites Hedy's provocation and
the fact that they were never made known to the public and thus cannot
constitute defamation.

[
5
]

The Court must decide if any of the actions
complained of constitute faults under the
Quebec Civil Code
or the
Charter
and,
if so, did those faults cause moral damages to Hedy.  Should any of Howard's
acts represent unlawful interference with Hedy's Charter rights, we must
determine if such interference was intentional, so as to warrant granting
punitive damages.

[
6
]

The Court is not seized of any question relating
to the validity of mother's will or of the heirs' rights under the estate.  The
will was not contested, but there is at least one other lawsuit pending between
the parties with respect to the estate.

THE WEBSITE

[
7
]

The Website
(Exhibit P-3)
is named
Hedystzoros.com, which means "Hedy's troubles" in Hebrew.  Howard
testified that he created it in April or May 2006 and took it off the Internet
on September 28
th
of that year.  It consists of five documents:

P-3A   an opening "Note to Hedy from her
siblings", reading:

Is money & material possessions so important (to you) that you
would abandon your community standards, your ethics, risk your reputation &
standing in your community & any normal relationship with your siblings?
If your answer is YES to any of the above, then you deserve everything you
get.  In that case you'll need luck & that's what we wish you.
;

P-3B   a letter to the three brothers from the Beth
Din reading:

"Re: Din Torah Blank vs. Rossdeutcher
[2]
.  Further to the various summons sent out
to Ms. H. Rossdeutcher, residing at (address stated, including postal code), as
the Beth Din has not received a satisfactory response from Ms. Rossdeutcher, we
hereby authorize you to handle this matter in any way which you see fit"
;

P-3C   a three-page letter Hedy wrote to her attorney
concerning the various issues between herself and her brothers, some of which
were the subject of pending lawsuits;

P-3D   extracts from mother's will showing all the
bequests and the naming of Hedy as liquidator;

P-3E   a letter from Hedy's attorney to Sheldon, a
rabbi living in Florida, concerning a dispute over the renting out of a parking
place annexed to the condo bequeathed to Hedy under mother's will.

[
8
]

Hedy's attorney argues that the publishing of
such documents over the Internet represents a violation of
articles 3
,
7
,
35

and
36(6)
of the
Civil Code
and
articles 4
,
5
and
9
of the
Charter
[3]
.
The Court agrees, adding that it also appears to violate article 36(2):
intentionally intercepting or using private communications.

[
9
]

Hedy is an Orthodox Jew.  She has earned her
livelihood for the past 35 years by teaching in an Orthodox Jewish school.  The
Hassidic community is very small and tight-knit, not only in Montreal but also,
it would seem, worldwide.  That Howard was appealing to this audience is clear
from document P-3A, where he uses the word "community" twice.  His
mention of abandoning her community standards and her ethics, and risking her
reputation & standing in that community target the core of Hedy's religious
and social life.  That is why the other documents in the Website are so
insidious.

[
10
]

Document P-3B, emanating from an important
Orthodox Jewish institution, also targets the Hassidic community.  It clearly
identifies Hedy, going so far as to state her home address down to the postal
code.  It states the she has not complied with the Beth Din's summonses, an act
that could be interpreted harshly by her peers.  The publication over the
Internet of such a document, dealing as it does with a private, family matter,
could have major consequences for Hedy, her husband and their six children.

[
11
]

It is true that Howard is one of the addressees
of the letter and that Hedy is not.  As a result, he argued that he had the
right to deal with it as he pleased.  The fact that it contains nominative
information could affect that right, but that argument was not raised before
us.

[
12
]

What was raised was article 7 Q.C.C.:
"No right may be exercised with the
intent of injuring another or in an excessive and unreasonable manner which is
contrary to the requirements of good faith"
.

[
13
]

Even assuming Howard had a certain right to
publicize a letter addressed to him, the Court is convinced that he did so here
with the intent of injuring Hedy.  We further analyze this point below but, for
present purposes, suffice it to say that, by including document P-3B in the
Website, he contravened article 7 and committed a civil fault.

[
14
]

The publication of document P-3C is indefensible
by all standards.  Not only does it not belong to Howard, it is also subject to
attorney-client privilege.  It is a blatant invasion of Hedy's privacy, as
described in article 36(2) and 36(6) Q.C.C., being a use of another's private
communications or correspondence.
Article 35
, paragraph 2 Q.C.C., proscribes
such acts, as does
section 9
of the
Charter
.  Howard violated these provisions
by publishing this document and thus committed a fault.

[
15
]

Concerning document P-3D, since mother's will is
in notarial form, no probate was necessary and it did not have to become
public.  As such, by putting parts of it on the Website that reveal the
bequests to Hedy and her appointment as liquidator, Howard has violated her
rights to respect for her private life and to non-disclosure of confidential
information.

[
16
]

Document P-3E does not appear to be of the same
importance as the others.  That said, it is a private communication and
correspondence that he is using without her permission and thus probably
constitutes a violation of article 7 Q.C.C.

[
17
]

Howard's attorney argued that he showed good
faith by cancelling the Website in compliance with Hedy's request to do so in
her lawyer's letter of September 5, 2006
(Exhibit P-5)
, but the facts
do not support such a conclusion.

[
18
]

Howard admitted that he cancelled the site on
September 28
th
.  However, the Court record shows that he received
service of the present action at 2:30 p.m. that day.  The Court concludes that,
by removing the Website, he did not so much comply with the lawyer's letter as
try to mitigate his exposure to damages after being sued.

[
19
]

In light of the above, in addition to the faults
we find under the
Civil Code
, the Court is also of the view that the Website
constitutes an unlawful interference with Hedy's rights and freedoms as
recognized in
sections 4
,
5
and
9
of the
Charter
.

[
20
]

Finally on this point, the fact that he might
not have publicized the existence of the Website does not erase these faults.
Hedy makes no claim for compensatory damages or defamation.  It was Howard
himself who advised her of the site's existence in late August 2006, an act
that smacks of an attempt to "rub it in".  It is partly on this basis
that Hedy claims moral damages, a question that we explore below.

THE CALL TO THE
PRINCIPAL

[
21
]

Howard's answers to questions on this topic were
evasive and misleading.  He initially testified that he called the school
probably in early 2006 and "
asked
someone at her school what the rules were for someone who did not attend at the
Beth Din
".  He stated that the rules he was
interested in were those that the Beth Din would apply, but this does not make
sense.  He was already in communication with that organisation and he could,
and undoubtedly did, obtain such enlightenment through its representatives.
Why contact an unrelated and probably uninformed third party for that purpose?

[
22
]

Eventually, he admitted that when he called the
school he asked to speak to the Principal, that he identified himself as Hedy's
brother and that he asked what the school would do to her in light of the fact
that she refused to comply with Jewish law and submit to the Beth Din.  The
Principal wisely - and correctly - replied that the school was bound by
provincial law and that this overrides the Beth Din's powers on employment
matters.

[
23
]

Howard clearly intended to cause Hedy problems
with her employer by making this call.  He knew that Hedy's job was the sole
source of income for her family, in light of her husband's serious illness.  He
knew that this type of school was careful to comply with Jewish law and
custom.  He knew that by undermining her reputation in one of the community's important
institutions, he would be damaging her reputation everywhere.

[
24
]

The intention to interfere with Hedy's right to
the safeguard of her honour, dignity and reputation and with her private life
by disclosing confidential information is evident.  This tactic fits nicely
into his on-going vendetta against her centered on mother's will.  His actions
in this regard constitute a fault under our general rules of extracontractual
liability, article 1457 Q.C.C., and an unlawful, and clearly intentional
interference with Hedy's rights and freedoms as recognized in
sections 4
,
5
and

9
of the
Charter
.

THE MESSAGES

[
25
]

Only three of Howard's phone messages were
produced
(Exhibit P-8,
including a sound recording)
, although Hedy testified
that when they actually spoke on other occasions the tenor was similar.  They
appear to be consecutive phone calls, perhaps with several minutes in between,
that were made in late November 2005, a couple of months after mother's death.
In them, Howard said some nasty things to his sister:

•

"… you pretend to be a religious
person.  It's shocking.  Your religion is money, nothing but money";

•

"… you made it so that your name is
going to be dragged through the mud";

•

"… you will be pursued, whether you
like it or not";

•

"… you know who was Ma's favourite
child?  Me.  It was me she called for in the hospital, not you. Not (others).
It was me.  And if you really want to know the truth, she didn't love you at
all.  You were her most despised child.  The reason why you did all –
everything that you did for her, which is really damn pitiful and minor, was
because you were trying to find favour.  And I don't blame you for trying to do
that because you are a real pathetic creature.  Really pathetic …";

•

"… Never in a million years … would I
have thought that a religious person like you would steal from her mother,
would manipulate and steal from her brothers.  You shame, you shamble.  You
think it's going to be a scandal?  It's going to be minor compared to what you
did, you being dragged through the streets by the Vaad (the Beth Din), you
deserve way worse than that.  Way, way, way worse than that".

[
26
]

He testified vaguely that he was reacting to
something Hedy had said to him and alleged that he was provoked.  In spite of
that, he could not remember what might have set him off and, more to the point,
he makes no mention of any such incident in the first Message.

[
27
]

The hate and malice in the Messages are
manifest, particularly when one hears them.  It is clear that they were left
with the intent of "injuring" Hedy, as proscribed by articles 7 and
1457 Q.C.C., as well as
section 4
of the
Charter
.  They demonstrate Howard's
desire for revenge.  The Court recognizes that these were private comments, but
that does not preclude them from constituting an intentional attack on Hedy's
dignity and honour, and thus forming part of the Court's considerations in the
decision on whether or not to impose punitive damages.

MORAL DAMAGES

[
28
]

Hedy claims $25,000 in moral damages for loss of
enjoyment of life, pain and suffering, distress, anxiety and psychological
damages.  The Court believes that she is entitled to them.

[
29
]

Regarding the Website, she expressed her horror
and shame at seeing it, leading her to worry over the loss of her job, over
possible problems for her six children to marry in the community, over social
ostracism for herself and her family and possible excommunication.

[
30
]

Moreover, at that time her husband was dying of
leukemia
[4]
and her mother, whom she considered to be her best friend, had died
less than a year before.  These factors are relevant.  "
One who commits a fault take his victim in
the state she is in when the damage is caused
"
[5]
.

[
31
]

Accordingly, even had Howard not been aware of
the other problems in Hedy's life that would exacerbate her moral damages, he
would still be liable for the increased damages.  The fact that he was very
much aware of them is a factor that will be considered in evaluating the
gravity of his fault for the purposes of punitive damages.

[
32
]

Hedy's testimony concerning the stress, anxiety
and fear that the Website caused her is quite believable, even though there is
no allegation of defamation.  As noted earlier, the importance of community
among Orthodox Jews cannot be overemphasized.  The Website clearly targeted her
community and it must have been devastating for her, particularly on a
religious and social level.  The financial shock probably came more with the
telephone call.

[
33
]

Hedy's husband had been ill with leukemia for
several years at the time of the telephone call to the Principal and was unable
to work.  Her teaching job was the main source of income for their large
family.  Howard's blatant attempt to have her terminated, for that is the
Court's conclusion, must have caused her great angst.

[
34
]

She testified that she suffered from loss of sleep,
trembling to the point of not being able to drive, paranoia, hives, migraines
and teeth gnashing when she could sleep.  The Court believes her and will award
her the full amount claimed of $25,000.  Any inducement to reduce the amount is
offset by our consideration of her emotional state at the time because of her
mother's recent death and her husband's terminal illness.  Interest and the
additional indemnity will run from the date of service: September 28, 2006.

PUNITIVE DAMAGES

[
35
]

The unlawful and intentional interference with a
right or freedom recognized by the
Charter
is one of the rare occasions in
Quebec law where punitive damages may be awarded:
section 49
,
paragraph 2
of
the Charter.  We have already identified numerous unlawful interferences with
Hedy's Charter rights by Howard.  We must now decide if they were intentional,
recognizing that the intentionality of the act itself is not the test but,
rather, the intentionality of the consequences of the act, i.e. the
interference with the Charter right
[6]
.

[
36
]

They clearly were.

[
37
]

Howard is an experienced businessman who runs
his own company.  When he chose the contents of the Website, he knew exactly
what he was doing.  In fact, his brothers did not agree with it and told him
that he was going too far.  Yet he persisted, knowing without a doubt that this
would result in an interference with Hedy's right to the safeguard of her
dignity, honour and reputation, with her right to respect for her private life
and with her right to the non-disclosure of confidential information.

[
38
]

This is what he wanted and intended because, by
doing so, he could most fully attain his objective: revenge.  The proof is
abundant that he was motivated by hate, malice and a desire for revenge.  Such
qualifiers are not necessary for us to grant punitive damages but, where they
apply, the finding of intentionality flows more easily.

[
39
]

As for the call to the Principal and the
Messages, we have already analyzed the intentionality in them and found it to
be very much present in both instances.  This is a case where punitive damages
should be imposed.

[
40
]

Hedy claims $50,000 under this heading.  Howard
admitted at trial that an amount up to $50,000 would be in conformity with the
financial criterion of article 1621 Q.C.C., but argued that, should the Court
see fit to order punitive damages, the amount should be less than that.  His
lawyer argued that the penalty should "
fit the crime
".

[
41
]

The
Civil Code
agrees with that position when it
directs us to consider the gravity of the debtor's fault, but the debtor's
fault is very serious here.  Moreover, it is aggravated by Howard's knowledge
that Hedy was experiencing other major difficulties in her life at that time,
i.e., dealing with the loss of her mother and the illness of her husband.

[
42
]

Nevertheless, the Court finds that, in light of
the moral damages awarded, the amount claimed is too high.  We set the punitive
damages at $25,000.  On such damages, interest and the additional indemnity run
only from the date of judgment
[7]
.

[
43
]

BASED ON
THESE REASONS, the court:

[
44
]

Grants

Plaintiff's action;

[
45
]

condemns
Defendant to pay to Plaintiff the sum of $25,000 in moral damages,
plus interest and the additional indemnity since September 28, 2006;

[
46
]

condemns
Defendant to pay to Plaintiff the sum of $25,000 in punitive
damages, with interest and the additional indemnity from the date of judgment;

[
47
]

the whole
with costs.

_____________________________

BRIAN RIORDAN, J.S.C.

Mtre. Elliott S. Brott

Attorney for Plaintiff

Mtre. Muriel Librati

Attorney for Defendant

Hearing Dates:  December
13 and 14, 2010

ANNEX "A"

CIVIL CODE OF QUEBEC

Art. 3.
Every person is
the holder of personality rights, such as the right to life, the right to the
inviolability and integrity of his person, and the right to the respect of his
name, reputation and privacy.

These rights are
inalienable.

Art. 7.
No right may be exercised with the
intent of injuring another or in an excessive and unreasonable manner which is
contrary to the requirements of good faith.

Art.
35.
Every person has a right to the respect of his reputation and privacy.

No one
may invade the privacy of a person without the consent of the person unless
authorized by law.

Art.
36.
The following acts, in particular, may be considered as invasions of
the privacy of a person:

…

(2)

intentionally intercepting or using his
private communications;

…

(6)
using
his correspondence, manuscripts or other personal documents.

CHARTER OF HUMAN
RIGHTS AND FREEDOMS

4.
Every person has a right to the
safeguard of his dignity, honour and reputation.

5.
Every person has a right to
respect for his private life.

9.
Every person has a right to
non-disclosure of confidential information.

49.
Any

unlawful
interference with any right or freedom recognized by this
Charter
entitles the
victim to obtain the cessation of such interference and compensation for the
moral or material prejudice resulting therefrom.

In case of unlawful and intentional interference
the tribunal may, in addition, condemn the person guilty of it to punitive
damages.

[1]
The Court will use the first names of the parties and their
brothers for ease of reference, given that they all have the same family name.
No disrespect is intended.

[2]
Rossdeutcher is Hedy's married name.

[3]
Reproduced in Annex "A" to this judgment.

[4]
He has since passed away.

la faute (prend) la victime dans l'état où elle se trouve au moment où le
dommage est causeé".  This is known as the
"thin skull rule".

Le syndicat national des employés de l'Hôpital

,
